label: copy-phase fed-back digit 2, early in recall (recall_idx 2-4)
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase, and only when the input token is the digit 2 (the model feeding back its own output 2). Within that, it is confined to early copy positions: recall_idx 2-4 (the 2 being original token 1-3). It is strongest when the 2 is original token 1, i.e. the step right after the first copied token (recall_idx 2, prev2_tok = <DEL>; 58% of mass, top examples are all of this form) and gets weaker at later positions. It is near-silent on the last output step (to_go 0) and on recall_idx 1 or 5 and later. It never fires on 2 during the original phase, on the delimiter, or on any other token, including the other digits. Missed activations are mostly weak, lowest-quartile ones.

issues: Minor: recall_idx 4 is a weak, unreliable tail, not a full member of the class. Precision there is only 0.53 on dev (0.44 at to_go 1, about 0.7 at to_go 2-4), and it holds just 4.7% of activation mass. Probing n_digits, digit identity of orig(0..2), prev_tok and in_count turned up no condition that separates the active cases from the inactive ones, so this looks like graded decay near threshold rather than a systematic class. It accounts for most of the 3933 test false positives.
recall_idx 2 and 3 with to_go >= 1 are nearly deterministic, with precision of about 1.0 in every to_go bucket. The explanation could state this more sharply.

Confirmed claims: activation is 100% copy phase, with zero activation on the original phase, the delimiter, or any input other than '2'. recall_idx 2 holds 57.8% of mass (prev2_tok = <DEL>). recall_idx 1: 6.5% rate, 0.2% mass. recall_idx >= 5: 0.4% precision, under 0.1% mass. to_go 0: 0.7% precision. All top examples are of the form 'x 2 ... <DEL> x [2]'.
The test misses (1280 steps, 0.3% of mass) are tiny activations, mostly at recall_idx 1 when the sequence starts with 2. This is scattered noise, not a systematic class.

Alternatives tried on test: dropping recall_idx 4 gave F1 0.876 (precision 1.0, recall 0.78). Requiring to_go >= 2 only at recall_idx 4 gave F1 0.936, essentially equal to the original 0.935. Neither is a meaningful improvement.
